_meta.purpose: Every load-bearing FACT in the spec, with its source, its rank on the content-bible §4 tie-break order, and its status. Consumed by the build's G5 copy-fidelity gate (verify-copy-fidelity.mjs), which reads facts[id].{verbatim, must_convey, pages}.

status_semantics.OWNER-RULED: Rank 1-2. The owner stated it. Load-bearing and usable as fact.
status_semantics.VERIFIED: Checked against its named source and it holds. Usable as fact, within the limits of its rank — a rank-3 VERIFIED fact is authoritative for what the brand SAYS, never for whether it is TRUE.
status_semantics.UNSUBSTANTIATED: Asserted as fact, but nothing at the required rank supports it. NOT usable as fact.
status_semantics.DISPUTED: Contested by evidence inside the spec itself, or asserts more than its source can support. NOT usable as fact.

_meta.rank_scale: content-bible.md §4: 1 owner-signed material (NONE supplied) · 2 owner direct written answers · 3 the client's own live site, snapshot-locked · 4 first-party competitor captures · 5 independent third parties · 6 agent inference. STANDING EXCEPTION: on any question of whether a CLAIM IS TRUE, rank 5 outranks rank 3.
_meta.provenance_of_pages_field: pages[] and defined_in are VERBATIM from the deterministic scan by scripts/gen-fact-registry.mjs — a literal read of which brief cites which D-* id. They were not hand-authored.
_meta.must_convey_policy: DELIBERATELY SPARSE, and the sparseness is a decision rather than an omission. must_convey is a HARD build-time requirement: verify-copy-fidelity.mjs blocks a page write when a required token is absent from the visible prose. It is populated ONLY where the token demonstrably must appear on EVERY page in pages[]. A dry run of the auto-extractor over this client produced actively harmful tokens — it emitted '100%' and '30%' for D-BRAND-RAILS-008 across 19 pages (those are the BANNED claims themselves, so the gate would have FORCED 19 pages to print the exact strings the doctrine forbids), plus intake LINE NUMBERS ('101' on 25 pages, '21,' on 21 pages) and the phrase 'founder pedigree', which belongs to a different client's vocabulary entirely. None of that was carried. Three facts carry a payload; the rest assert none and are therefore skipped by the gate rather than falsely enforced.
_meta.canonical_value_policy: canonical_value is BUILD-CONSUMED: verify-copy-fidelity.mjs reads it into its canonical blob and into its failure text, and any copy agent reading this registry reads it as 'the value of this fact'. RELYING ON THE STATUS FLAG ALONE TO STOP AN UNUSABLE CLAIM IS FAIL-OPEN — a build that reads canonical_value without checking status ships the string. THE RULE, applied 2026-08-12: no row may carry, in canonical_value, a claim about the world that its own status marks unusable, or a string the content doctrine bans. Such rows carry canonical_value:null — which is the generator's own no-derivable-value output (gen-fact-registry.mjs emits `canonical_value: canonical_value || null`) and which the consumer skips, since a falsy canonical_value is neither enforced nor printed. NULLING CANNOT WEAKEN THE G5 GATE: that gate enforces `verbatim` and `must_convey` ONLY. The banned or unverified string survives afterwards ONLY inside `statement` / `note` as a labelled QUARANTINE RECORD — a ban list must be able to name what it bans — never inside a value slot. Rows whose canonical_value is an internal direction, a decision-accounting row or an absence record rather than a world-claim keep their value.
_meta.synthetic_rows: Rows flagged registry_of_record:true are load-bearing claims that no brief cites by a D-* id — the canonical NAP and the §G-6 proof families. They carry verbatim:null and must_convey:[] so they can never gate a build write; their pages[] documents REACH only. Their enforcement lives in client-rules.json.

THE TWO HALVES MUST BE STATED TOGETHER AND NEVER COLLAPSED INTO ONE VERDICT. PART 1 — THE COPY DEFECT IS FIXED, AND IT IS MACHINE-ENFORCED RATHER THAN MERELY AGREED: the assertion forms are banned site-wide by the bannedContent operated-pause entry in client-rules.json (added 2026-08-12; this claim previously had NO machine mirror anywhere in that file), attribution is compelled by requiredPairings.RP-7, capabilityTruth.operated-pause-precedent is false, content-bible §3b line 78 carries the standalone prohibition, all 6 pause-carrying briefs carry the ⚠OWNER PLACEHOLDER, and positioning-plan.md §5's 'Verified precedent' label was corrected upstream. THE ONE STATED COVERAGE LIMIT, recorded rather than hidden: a bare UNATTRIBUTED retelling is not mechanically caught, because a pattern that caught it would also false-block the attributed report briefs/guarantee.md:126 permits — that residue is an authoring rule (RP-7 + the placeholders), not a compiled gate. PART 2 — THE BLOCKER WAS STILL OPEN AT THIS WRITING, AND IS NOW WAIVED (2026-08-12, owner election), because what is missing is not wording but CONFIRMATION ONLY THE OWNER CAN GIVE — and the waiver did not supply it. readiness-verdict.md:90 states the closure condition in full: 'Confirmation the billing pause was actually operated — which account, which months, client consent to reference it. Clears 13. If unconfirmable, the sentence is deleted from 6 pages.' It has not arrived. A FIXED DEFECT IS NOT A CLOSED BLOCKER — banning the assertion proves the spec will not claim the event; it does not establish that the event happened. ⚠ AND A WAIVED BLOCKER IS NOT A CONFIRMED EVENT: the 2026-08-12 waiver removed this from blocker_count without confirming anything, so the assertion stays banned in every surface. Anything reporting only Part 1 is reporting half of this row. CANONICAL_VALUE NULLED 2026-08-12: this row previously carried, in both statement and canonical_value, the assertion 'The billing pause has already been operated on a live account' as a usable value across 6 pages' reach. canonical_value is build-consumed, so the DISPUTED status alone was FAIL-OPEN. THE DISTINCTION THE WHOLE BLOCKER TURNS ON: what is verified is that the SENTENCE EXISTS in the snapshot; that the EVENT HAPPENED is not. Its only source is one sentence of the client's own rank-3 marketing copy. NOT AT ISSUE, AND NOT TO BE WEAKENED: the offer MECHANIC (decisions-ledger D-003, carried here by D-OFFER-003 and D-POSITION-W1) — an agreed monthly retainer, assessed month by month against the agreed metrics, billing pauses off-target and resumes when results are back on track, and the work continues throughout — is OWNER-RULED and fully publishable today on that ruling alone. Only the claim that it has already been EXERCISED is unverified. ⚠ AND AS OF 2026-08-12 THAT RULING SITS ON MUCH FIRMER GROUND: the owner was shown the competing TERMINAL reading of 'or you don't pay' and ELECTED the monthly pause-and-resume in a durable rank-2 artifact (_inbox/2026-08-12-owner-rulings.md), closing readiness blocker 3. D-003 no longer rests on an agent's transcription of a chat message. That strengthens the MECHANIC and changes nothing in this row — the EXERCISED-ALREADY claim is still unverified and still banned as an assertion. PERMITTED HANDLING until the owner confirms, with briefs/industries-law-firm.md §4 as the SSOT: report what the current site SAYS, visibly flagged as unconfirmed and never as proof — or omit it. Do not narrate it as a case, do not date it, do not imply a real invoice was ever paused. A DE-IDENTIFIED RETELLING DOES NOT FIX THIS: de-identifying protects the CLIENT, it does not evidence the EVENT, and a de-identified account still asserts that the event occurred. HISTORY, restated rather than deleted: it shipped as a VERIFIED fact on 6 pages off a rank-3 source, and positioning-plan.md §5 called it 'Verified precedent', which CONFLATED 'a string exists in the snapshot' with 'the event happened' — an authoring error, not an inherited one. READINESS BLOCKER 7 — FIXED UPSTREAM 2026-08-12. The history is restated, not deleted. THE DEFECT: the content bible's own §2 'SAFE' replacement row was authored as 'Every [vertical] campaign we have run under the guarantee reached first page within the guarantee window', which WAS ITSELF AN ABSOLUTE CLAIM of the banned shape — an authoring error made inside this spec, not a string inherited from the live site, and it had been authorised site-wide. THE FIX, APPLIED: content-bible §2 row 1 was REWRITTEN on 2026-08-12 and now reads 'Between [start month/year] and [end month/year] we ran [n] [vertical] campaigns under the guarantee; [k] of them reached first page on the contracted key phrases inside the agreed window' — a BOUNDED, DATED COUNT, never a rate. That row now additionally bans, inside that sentence, 'every', 'all', 'always', '100%', 'success rate', and any restatement of k/n as a percentage or ratio; requires n, k, the period and the measurement source to be disclosed together; holds the k = n case to '[n] of [n], between [dates]' with no generalisation past that closed dated set and no projection forward to a prospect; and DROPS the row rather than softening it if n, k or the period cannot be disclosed. The superseded wording must not be reinstated. WHAT THE REWRITE DID NOT CHANGE — THIS ROW'S STATUS: it fixed the SHAPE of the safe version, not the EVIDENCE behind the claim family. The §G-6.1 dataset has still not landed in _inbox/, so this fact remains UNSUBSTANTIATED and even the bounded, dated form is unpublishable until n, k, the period and the measurement source actually exist. client-rules.json bans the SHAPE rather than a wording, so the ban held across the rewrite and holds whichever wording is chosen.
